messages.subject: Re: [oscr] Incorporate occasion covariates
parts:
Hi Giacomo,

Yes, those covariates should go into the tdf, with a naming convention like "doy.1", "doy.2",... "doy.24" and "temp.1", "temp.2",... "temp.24" and so on numbered from occasion 1 to 24.  That convention could also be used for temporal covariates that do not vary by trap (i.e., all traps have the same value but values differ across occasions).  For covariates that vary by trap but are static across time, the number is dropped (e.g., "habitat").

On Mon, Jan 15, 2024 at 5:22 AM Giacomo Rosa <rosagi...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi,

I’m working on a two years CMR data of a subterranean population of Strinati’s cave salamander. I already posted a question regarding the analysis of this dataset (https://groups.google.com/g/oscr_package/c/vbZ1OqfQe6A), to which Andy Royle kindly replied, allowing me to solve the problem and successfully run the models.

Now, I would like to add the day of the year and the air temperature at the entrance, the middle and the bottom of the cave for each sampling occasion, in order to model the detection probability of animals, but I don't know how to treat these "occasion-covariates". Should I insert them in the tdf as trap-covariates or in the edf?
I think that I have to add them as trapcovs, but I don't know how to organize the new dataset. Do I have to add a column for each sampling occasion (e.g, I have 24 sampling opportunities, so 24 columns for the day of the year, 24 for the temperature at the entrance and so on)?

Thank you very much for your help and  for creating this group!

Giacomo Rosa
